title: Kaze
description: A highland meadow in July under small fair-weather cumulus, and the wind is yours. Brush across the grass and your stroke becomes a gust: it runs out across the field, slowing and narrowing as it goes, the grass lies over under it and springs back, and the meadow shows honami, the bright waves where bent blades turn their glossy faces to the sky. Behind, the clouds drift by their distance and lean a little after your gusts. Left alone, a light breeze keeps moving through.
intent: Technique 10, Kaze (factory/reality/techniques.md): an Eulerian motion field you author live. A 96x40 stable-fluids velocity grid (Stam 1999, https://www.dgp.toronto.edu/public_user/stam/reality/Research/pdf/ns.pdf) carries the air in metres per second on the ground, rescaled by perspective as it moves; the grass is a field of damped springs driven by dynamic pressure; the visible wave is a Kajiya-Kay sheen on the blade tangent (MoGe-2 canopy normal tilted by the bend), applied as the change from rest so the still meadow is the photograph; fine gust streaks and the cumulus drift are two-phase flow maps (Vlachos 2010) so nothing smears or seams. ?gust=demo throws a scripted gust, ?t=seconds runs the wind that long and holds it, ?breeze=0..2 scales the idle air, ?debug=bend overlays the bend field.

sources.author: Syuhei Inoue, Unsplash
sources.note: Highland meadow (Kirigamine-like plateau, Nagano), 5561x3707, worked at 2400x1600. Sky matte by a column scan (tools/depth/bakes/kaze/skymask.py) on Depth Anything V2 Small depth (tools/depth/depth_hr.py); sky plate filled below the skyline by push-pull; normals, metric depth and FOV (93.8 deg) from MoGe-2 ViT-S (tools/depth/normals.py); trees found as large dark blobs. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/bake.py.
